decision: Retire the current R=3 patchwise finite-model class and map a support-radius versus prime-side-cost dual frontier before further primal optimization.

next_problem.dual_frontier: For each R, basis dictionary, and theorem-object set, find the strongest stable all-patch dual lower bound.
next_problem.prime_cost: Derive and benchmark the exact support-to-prime cutoff relation for the active Fourier convention.
next_problem.gating_rule: Do not run an expensive nonconvex primal search when a stable dual lower bound is at least 1.
next_problem.certification_rule: Keep rational finite-model positivity separate from interval transfer, count theorems, and tail theorems.

work_packages.task: Sweep support radii 4.5 through 9 with multiple basis densities and width schedules; compute single-band, three-band, and five-band dual bounds.
Run primal searches only for configurations passing the dual gate, using multi-point patch constraints and independent mesh refinement.
Implement and benchmark a segmented prime-power accumulator with explicit cutoff and error budgets.
Replace the A1 count and tail prototypes by cited, directed-rounded theorem objects.
Rationalize or interval-enclose any stable frontier witness and preserve the no-known-zero fitting discipline.

do_not_do: Do not increase Burer-Monteiro rank at R=3.
Do not infer primal feasibility from center-only dual escape.
Do not launch the largest prime cutoff before a dual gate passes.
Do not fit or select candidates using known zeta-zero ordinates.
Do not promote finite rational surrogate positivity to an RH claim.

success_criteria.research: Find at least one all-patch configuration with stable dual lower bounds below 1 and a quantified prime-side execution plan.
success_criteria.constructive: Produce a full-patch primal candidate below the same finite budget.
success_criteria.upgrade: Interval-transfer the transform, count, and tail objects needed by any surviving witness or candidate.
